title: 📋 Know Your Exam Inside Out

sections.heading: Why this matters
sections.body: Students who understand the exam format score higher — not because the questions are easier, but because they manage time better, know what's expected, and don't waste energy being confused by instructions.

sections.heading: IELTS overview
sections.body:
🎧 Listening: 30 min + 10 min transfer = 40 questions
👁️ Reading: 60 min = 40 questions across 3 passages
✍️ Writing: 60 min = Task 1 (150+ words) + Task 2 (250+ words)
🗣️ Speaking: 11–14 min = 3 parts

highlight: Academic and General Training tests differ in Reading and Writing Task 1. Always confirm which you're taking!

question: How many sections does the IELTS Listening test have?
explanation:
The 4 sections increase in difficulty:
Section 1: Everyday conversation (e.g. booking a service)
Section 2: Monologue about everyday topic (e.g. tour guide)
Section 3: Discussion in educational/training context
Section 4: Academic lecture or talk
hint: Think about how IELTS progressively gets harder through the test.

instruction: Match each IELTS section to its correct time allocation:
explanation:
Total test time: approximately 2h 45min (not including speaking, which is usually on a different day).

Reading and Writing are both 60 minutes but completely different tasks — Reading is comprehension, Writing is production.

title: 🎯 The 4 IELTS Writing Criteria
body:
Each criterion is worth exactly 25% of your Writing score:

🎯 Task Achievement (Task 2) / Task Response (Task 1)
→ Did you answer ALL parts of the question?

🔗 Coherence & Cohesion
→ Is your writing logically organised with clear paragraphing?

📚 Lexical Resource
→ Do you use a RANGE of vocabulary accurately?

⚡ Grammatical Range & Accuracy
→ Do you use VARIED structures with few errors?

quick.label: Missing any criterion tanks your overall score

question: In IELTS Speaking, what does the examiner assess in Part 2?
options: Fluency, Lexical Resource, Grammar, and Pronunciation equally
correct: Fluency, Lexical Resource, Grammar, and Pronunciation equally
explanation:
All 4 criteria are assessed equally (25% each) throughout the entire speaking test:
• Fluency & Coherence
• Lexical Resource
• Grammatical Range & Accuracy
• Pronunciation

Not just in Part 2 — all parts are assessed on all criteria.
hint: The speaking criteria mirror the writing criteria but include Pronunciation instead of Task Achievement.

sentence: In IELTS Task 1, you should spend approximately _____ minutes and write at least _____ words.
explanation:
Task 1 = 20 minutes, 150+ words
Task 2 = 40 minutes, 250+ words

Why 40 minutes for Task 2? Because it's worth more marks — roughly double the mark allocation of Task 1. Always do Task 2 first if you're running short on time.
hint: Task 2 gets 40 minutes and 250 words — Task 1 gets half that.

question: What does "Not Given" mean in IELTS Reading True/False/Not Given questions?
options: The information is not mentioned anywhere in the passage
correct: The information is not mentioned anywhere in the passage
explanation:
"Not Given" is the most misunderstood answer type.

NOT GIVEN = the passage simply does not address this topic
FALSE = the passage says the OPPOSITE

Common trap: students see "Not Given" and think "well that seems unlikely to be true, so it must be False." Wrong — your outside knowledge is irrelevant. Only what the TEXT says matters.
hint: Ask yourself: "Does the passage address this topic at all?" Not: "Is this true in real life?"
